features: context odds minus median of up to two surrounding scores per side
content overlap with both neighboring sentences

method.advance: At least six novel report localizations across both generators and both report lengths, plus at least two novel localizations across scholarly works, at most two additional genuine groups in any cohort, and at least 90 percent assessed coverage. All evaluation cases already have project exposure. A passing method needs a fresh panel before serving.
method.fit: 20 previously used GAO report works. Train work-balanced regularized linear heads on unchanged and publisher-edited exact native sentence targets. Byte-identical edited versions contribute no extra observations.
method.metric: Strict localization is at least half of all edited nonspace characters and at least .30 intersection over union in one reported range. Comparators are existing first six native primary contexts at .50, plus the reported long position check for F1000Research and eLife.
method.point: Strictly above the second-highest original-work maximum in each of two length bands. Use 24 consumed short-report originals and 16 consumed long-report originals, disjoint from fit and assessment works.
method.proposal: Select one native sentence of at least 40 nonspace characters or one run of up to six such sentences in the same paragraph. Short files (up to eight sentences) use only single sentences. Longer files use a length-normalized sum with a .015 cost per added sentence. Abstain on a tied top range.
method.supervision: Binary and intensity heads use the same three uncalibrated context features. The binary target is any annotated edit in the sentence. The intensity target is the fraction of sentence word tokens both inside an annotation and outside a monotonic exact word alignment with the original. A third arm adds the fixed text-only features. The source original is used for labels only.
